units.html: Proof-of-Work (PoW) is the foundational consensus mechanism of the MAGNE Layer1 network. It relies on computational competition to ensure decentralized trust, secure transaction validation, and network resistance against censorship. Each node must solve cryptographic puzzles to earn block proposal rights, eliminating reliance on trusted intermediaries. At MAGNE.AI, PoW has been reimagined beyond traditional high-energy mining. By integrating with DePin (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure), edge devices like smartphones become mining nodes. This makes consensus participatory and accessible to anyone, aligning network growth with real-world usage. The ultimate vision for MAGNE’s PoW is to create a trustless, mobile-first, and highly secure Layer1 infrastructure for Web3.

units.html: Unlike traditional mining that depends on specialized hardware and high energy consumption, MAGNE Layer1 introduces a lightweight form of PoW: mobile mining. Equipped with secure SPU and NPU chips, MAGNE.AI devices allow everyday users to contribute idle computing resources, verify transactions, and earn rewards—ushering in a truly inclusive consensus layer. This is powered by MAGNE’s proprietary DePin infrastructure, where every physical device becomes a node in the blockchain, contributing not just as a user but as a validator of network security. Such participatory design reduces entry barriers to Web3 while enabling more equitable value distribution. By fusing PoW with edge hardware, MAGNE redefines the consensus model for a decentralized future.

units.html: In MAGNE Layer1, PoW serves not only as the cornerstone of consensus, but also as a performance accelerator. The project introduces deep architectural enhancements to the EVM by simplifying Merkle Tree structures and integrating intelligent caching. This enables state data to be accessed with minimal disk I/O, improving execution speed. Smart contracts benefit from lower latency and higher throughput, making the network suitable for high-frequency applications. Furthermore, this foundational design aligns with future Layer2 expansion, ensuring smooth data synchronization across modular chains. In MAGNE, PoW is both a shield and an engine—safeguarding the chain while elevating its capabilities.

units.html: Inspired by architectures like Berachain’s Proof-of-Liquidity, MAGNE decouples consensus from governance. PoW is strictly focused on securing the network, while decision-making and voting are governed through the MHA token on-chain. This separation of responsibilities allows Layer1 to focus on performance and security, while granting governance power to the broader community—avoiding centralization risks where miners dominate protocol control.

units.html: Why M Hash Layer2 is Built on OP Stack
units.text: Why M Hash Layer2 is Built on OP Stack

units.html: Before building M Hash Layer2, our team conducted extensive research and evaluation of available Layer 2 frameworks. We ultimately chose the OP Stack as the foundation for M Hash Layer2 Rollup because of its modularity, high performance potential, and alignment with our goals.
units.text: Before building M Hash Layer2, our team conducted extensive research and evaluation of available Layer 2 frameworks. We ultimately chose the OP Stack as the foundation for M Hash Layer2 Rollup because of its modularity, high performance potential, and alignment with our goals.

units.html: Achieve up to 100M gas per second throughput. We optimized EVM execution, state storage, and transaction handling to push the upper limits of Layer 2 performance.
units.text: Achieve up to 100M gas per second throughput. We optimized EVM execution, state storage, and transaction handling to push the upper limits of Layer 2 performance.

units.html: Deliver an extremely low-cost rollup solution. Since Layer 1 calldata costs dominate rollup fees, we designed M Hash Layer2 to support flexible Data Availability (DA) layers beyond mainnet posting—significantly reducing gas overhead.
units.text: Deliver an extremely low-cost rollup solution. Since Layer 1 calldata costs dominate rollup fees, we designed M Hash Layer2 to support flexible Data Availability (DA) layers beyond mainnet posting—significantly reducing gas overhead.

units.html: Contribute to open infrastructure. All performance optimizations and research from M Hash Layer2 will be open-sourced and shared with the broader OP Stack ecosystem.

units.html: Modular Execution Clients: OP Stack allows M Hash Layer2 to plug in different execution clients for performance tuning or decentralization. We can integrate with existing BSC-compatible clients or build our own execution layer.
units.text: Modular Execution Clients: OP Stack allows M Hash Layer2 to plug in different execution clients for performance tuning or decentralization. We can integrate with existing BSC-compatible clients or build our own execution layer.

units.html: Layer 1 (L1) is the base settlement and security layer responsible for data propagation and consensus — in our ecosystem, this is MAGNE (PoW, native token $MHA). units.html: To maximize throughput and reduce gas fees on M Hash Layer2 Rollup, we introduced multiple performance optimizations across the Execution and Derivation layers of the OP Stack. These enhancements build upon research and engineering efforts tailored to high-throughput Layer 2 networks.

units.html: In M Hash Layer2, we optimized how the EVM accesses state by improving cache hierarchy. Similar to BSC’s "SharedPool" concept, we introduced a Level 1.5 (L1.5) cache to improve data access efficiency between in-memory and dik-level storage, reducing latency in execution.
units.text: In M Hash Layer2, we optimized how the EVM accesses state by improving cache hierarchy. Similar to BSC’s "SharedPool" concept, we introduced a Level 1.5 (L1.5) cache to improve data access efficiency between in-memory and dik-level storage, reducing latency in execution.

units.html: Improved Bloom Filter Accuracy in Diff Layer
units.text: Improved Bloom Filter Accuracy in Diff Layer

units.html: Bloom filters are used to check the presence of key-value pairs during state lookups. However, large datasets increase false positives. M Hash Layer2 reduces the Diff Layer depth from 128 to 32, shrinking the filter’s data footprint and cutting down on unnecessary recursive cache lookups. This significantly improves EVM state retrieval efficiency.

Previously, separate caches between the main and prefetch threads limited performance. We now use a shared world state pool (originStorage), allowing both threads to access L1.5 cache directly. This design dramatically improves cache hit rates during block processing.

units.html: The opgas node executes block transactions in batches without requiring confirmation of each individual operation. Once a batch is complete, the opnode verifies the entire set in one consensus step. This asynchronous batch processing design breaks the traditional synchronous execution bottleneck, making it ideal for high-performance applications such as trading platforms, blockchain games, social apps, and payment solutions.
